rules.text: never schedule **Sunday, Monday, or Saturday**. Monday is held open as an emergency reserve. Work is booked **Tuesday–Friday** only.
details: "Today" is never used either — except a job whose stated preferred date is today, or a past-due job that needs the soonest slot.

rules.text: roughly **8:00 AM – 5:30 PM Pacific**. Times are stored with the Pacific time-zone offset (e.g. `2026-06-25T09:00:00-07:00`).

**Fill the nearest open days first**, packing densely from 8 AM, then a daily **compaction pass** pulls later jobs into the earliest open slots. Keep about a **30-minute buffer** between jobs and never double-book a tech.
details: Busy time is read from the tech's **entire** calendar (including turns), so it never books on top of an all-day turn.
Compaction is idempotent — once everything is packed, a re-run changes nothing.

rules.text: Emergency / Urgent → High → Normal / Medium → Low.
if a job's scheduled time passes without completion, reschedule it to the next available slot (keeping priority order). Never leave a past-due job unscheduled.

Emergency and Urgent melds are sorted to the front of the queue and scheduled on today's date (the current day), overriding the Monday and "no today" restrictions. All other melds continue to respect the Tue–Fri rule and never land on today.
details: **Always goes first, never bumped to another date (rewritten 2026-07-02, both Tacoma and Spokane):** the emergency takes the earliest available slot on today's calendar — never just wedged into whatever gap happens to be free. Whatever else is already on today's calendar shifts LATER that same day to make room; an already-committed today appointment is never moved to a different date (the resident is expecting the tech today regardless). Today's close can stretch past the normal close time to fit everyone in — see each region's section below for its specific allowance. A today job with a stated resident preference/lock is never shifted.

**Weekend exception (fixed 2026-07-12):** if "today" is Saturday or Sunday, the emergency is NOT booked on the weekend — nobody works it. Instead it's redirected to **Monday, first thing**, with the exact same "goes first, pushes everything else later that same day" behavior, just landing on Monday instead of today. (Previously the code had a bug where `insertEmergencyToday` booked straight onto the weekend date whenever a run happened to fall on Sat/Sun — found 2026-07-12 when 7 emergency melds landed on a Sunday. Fixed in both `pm_scheduler.js` and `pm_spokane_scheduler.js` via a `nextMonday()` redirect.)

rules.text: **Preference lock — honor a stated day/time/date.** If a work order's **title or chat** asks for a specific day, time, or date, the scheduler books it there and won't move it.
details: Locked jobs are exempt from compaction, blocked-day moves, and overlap moves — a stated preference is never overridden by packing.
Ordinal dates are understood ("June 18th"). A stated date of **today** books same-day; a date in the **past** is dropped (job scheduled ASAP).
Only the **title** and a genuine **chat request** count — office-hours boilerplate ("Mon–Fri 9–5") is never treated as a preference.

**Weekend/Monday exception (added 2026-07-09, extended to managers 2026-07-16):** a stated Saturday/Sunday/Monday date from the **resident, the tech, OR a manager** (e.g. a tech rescheduling around an emergency and offering to come Saturday, or a manager writing "please schedule Monday July 20th") is honored as a preference — this is the only way work lands on a reserved day. Originally resident-only, then opened to the tech's own stated day, now a manager's direct instruction counts too.

`nextOccurrenceOfDay` (both `pm_scheduler.js` and `pm_spokane_scheduler.js`) used to have a hardcoded block making "Monday" impossible to resolve as a target day even when explicitly requested — fixed 2026-07-16 so a stated Monday preference can actually be honored, not just silently dropped.

A chat-based preference normally only lives ~26h (anti-thrash — see below), which isn't enough to *permanently* protect a meld sitting on a reserved day. `hasReservedDayOverride()` in both scripts scans the **full** comment history (ignoring recency) for a resident/tech/manager message naming that specific day/date, and — without ever triggering a reschedule itself — permanently suppresses the reserved-day relocation once found. This is what makes a manager's one-time chat note as durable as a title-embedded date.

The standard "outside business hours" auto-reply text (which itself says "Monday–Friday") is explicitly excluded from all of this matching — otherwise the auto-reply's own mention of "Monday" reads as a manager stating a preference on every after-hours meld.

rules.text: **Reads the chat.** It reads each job's recent messages for reschedule requests, resident preferred times, and duration hints, and accommodates residents when possible (without overriding Emergency/Urgent).
details: A Claude "chat reader" interprets the intent; the code still applies every rule above. If it's unavailable, a keyword reader is the fallback.

**Not-yet-scheduled** jobs honor requests from the last **30 days**; **already-scheduled** jobs only act on messages from the last **~26 hours** (so an old message doesn't re-shuffle the calendar every day) — except the reserved-day override above, which is recency-exempt by design.
"Earlier / sooner / before Monday" means **avoid** that day and find an earlier slot — not book on it.
Duration hints are only trusted between **15 minutes and 4 hours** (avoids reading "within 48 hours" as a 48-hour job).

rules.text: **Append-only — the set schedule NEVER moves (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-17).** Once anything is placed it stays put: **in-house work does not move, vendor work does not move, and available dates do not move.** The scheduler only **adds** newly-created work into the **next available open slots** — it never reschedules, repacks, or pulls existing work earlier, not even for a high-priority or high-demand unit. If a unit is already scheduled late, it stays late; the way to make future units land sooner is to create/schedule the turn earlier, not to re-shuffle what's already set. Priority order (below) only sequences **new, unscheduled** work among itself — it never displaces work that's already on the calendar. (This overrides any earlier "REPACK"/priority-pull idea for pulling a late turn forward.) The **one exception** is a **cancelled move-out** (see Turns): a turn whose move-out/notice was cancelled is a *void* turn, so it's deleted outright and the slot it frees is backfilled by the next-priority unscheduled turn — that's reclaiming an invalid slot, not rescheduling valid work.
don't reshuffle without a reason — only move work for a higher priority, a past-due job, or a valid resident conflict.

any appointment that lands on a reserved day (Mon/Sat/Sun) or that double-books a tech is automatically relocated — unless it's backed by a stated preference lock (see the weekend exception above), which is left alone.

**Manual assignment is sacred (firm rule, Florencia 2026-07-22, the MOST important rule alongside the one below) — applies in every region, no exceptions.** Once a meld has ANY assignee — a technician (even one outside that region's normal pool) OR a vendor — no scheduler ever takes it away or hands it to someone else. Only a genuinely unassigned meld (no in-house servicer, no active vendor request) is ever auto-claimed.
details: **Vendor assignments are easy to miss:** they live in the `vendor_assignment_requests` field, a SEPARATE field from `in_house_servicers`. A meld handed to a vendor still shows an *empty* `in_house_servicers` list, so any check that only looks at `in_house_servicers` sees it as "unassigned" and will silently steal it back for a technician. **Real incident (2026-07-22):** this happened in Tri-Cities — assigning a meld to a vendor got it silently un-assigned and handed back to Jared/Jaxson. Fixed the same day in all three repair schedulers (`pm_scheduler.js`, `pm_spokane_scheduler.js`, `pm_tricities_scheduler.js`) via a shared `hasActiveVendorAssignment()` check (a vendor request counts as active unless it's `rejected` or `canceled`).

Tacoma used to have a "steal it back for Jonas" branch for a meld sitting on a tech who doesn't work Tacoma (e.g. Margarito). **Removed 2026-07-22** as part of this same rule — Tacoma now only ever claims a truly unassigned meld, matching Spokane's convention (a8e392f, 2026-07-20) and Tri-Cities.

rules.text: **Manual appointment moves are sacred (firm rule, Florencia 2026-07-20, made universal 2026-07-22) — applies in every region, no exceptions.** If a person moves a meld's appointment by hand in the PropertyMeld UI, no scheduler ever touches that appointment again — not via compaction, emergency-insertion displacement, or the reserved-day/overlap self-heal. Every scheduler always logs in as the same "Ridgeview Scheduler" service account (persona id **62267**); every appointment carries an `update_by`/`create_by` persona id, so if the last touch came from a *different* persona, a human did it by hand. Implemented as `wasManuallyMoved()` in all three repair schedulers (`pm_scheduler.js`, `pm_spokane_scheduler.js`, `pm_tricities_scheduler.js`) as of 2026-07-22 — previously Spokane-only.
always dry-run a change first. Live runs happen only in the cloud (see "How it runs").
**Only Jonas Hoard and Armani Mitchell work Tacoma.** Jonas takes all non-turn repairs; Armani takes turns.
details: Any non-turn tc68/tc34 job found on a different tech is **reassigned to Jonas** (e.g. Margarito is Tri-Cities, not Tacoma).

rules.text: **Jonas does every work type here, including lawn / Environmental** — unlike Spokane, grounds work at tc68/tc34 is not split off to anyone else.

**Grounds recurring melds default to Friday (added 2026-07-16, Jonas's request).** All of Tacoma's recurring melds (`recurring_meld` set on the meld) are grounds work, so every recurring instance defaults to a Friday preference lock, business hours, if it doesn't already have a more specific stated preference from the title/chat. A stated preference still wins — the Friday default only fills in when none is found.
**Turns** (project melds) go to Armani; the repair scheduler leaves them alone. (Dulce Salinas legitimately appears on "AppFolio Estimate" turn melds.)

**Emergency/Urgent extended close: 7pm** (`EMERGENCY_EXTENDED_CLOSE` in `pm_scheduler.js`) — same +2h allowance over Tacoma's normal 5pm close that Spokane uses over its own. No property clustering here, so every shift (emergency vs. whatever it displaces) uses the flat 0.5h buffer — there's no same-property exception like Spokane's.

**Justin Gutierrez + Jacob Jett split repairs by PROPERTY (Jacob hired 2026-07-20, replacing Wade Hippen).** A property is decided fresh each run: any property with an Emergency/Urgent/High in-scope meld belongs to Justin; a property where every in-scope meld is Medium/Normal/Low belongs to Jacob. This only decides a NEW/unassigned/reclaimed meld — one that already has a tech is never reassigned. A reclaimed-from-Wade meld routes through this same rule (no longer blanket-to-Justin).

**Justin's day ends at 4:00 PM**, not the general 5:00 PM cutoff — no job is scheduled to end after 16:00 (requested by Justin, 2026-07-01). A hard-pinned title/chat date that doesn't fit with the normal buffer gets squeezed in with a tighter (or zero) buffer that day instead of running the day later — the close time never moves, even for a non-negotiable date. (Jacob has no stated close-time exception yet — uses the general 5pm baseline until he asks for one.)
**Covers** the Spokane property group plus Our Natural Homes.
turns, Environmental (those go to the grounds team), and pest. Unassigned pest is never auto-assigned.
**Only reclaim** a repair from the turn techs (Scott Higley, Ron Cramer, Micheal Magoon) when they're wrongly holding a plain repair, or from unassigned non-pest jobs.
details: **Leave alone:** David & Alexander (grounds), **Florencia** (pest), and Dulce (estimates) — those assignments are intentional.

rules.text: when a job needs the tenant present, the scheduler reads the tenant's chosen availability windows and books inside one.
**Pest "attend treatment" jobs** are date-pinned: the date is fixed and the exact time is vendor-driven (left to a person).
Only **one appointment per job** is kept — duplicate appointments are cleaned up so they can't cause double-booking.

rules.category: Emergency/Urgent always goes FIRST on today's calendar (rewritten 2026-07-02)
rules.text: an emergency is never wedged into whatever gap happens to be free — it takes the earliest available time today, and whatever else is already on today's calendar shifts LATER that same day to make room (`insertEmergencyToday`). An already-committed today appointment is **never** moved to a different date for this — the resident is expecting Justin today regardless, so the day's close time can stretch past the normal 4pm, up to **6pm** (`EMERGENCY_EXTENDED_CLOSE`), instead. A today job with a stated resident preference/lock is left in place, never shifted.
details: **An Emergency/Urgent meld already sitting on today is left alone (fixed 2026-07-20).** It used to get needlessly re-run through `insertEmergencyToday` whenever today is a reserved day (e.g. Monday) or it overlapped another same-day meld — neither check knew about the emergency-today exception. With several real same-day emergencies each re-triggering this against the others, times cascaded unbounded (a real incident produced invalid post-midnight hours like "37:00" from 9 simultaneous same-day Emergency melds). Both the reserved-day and overlap checks now skip an Emergency/Urgent meld whose appointment is already today — a genuine today-vs-today double-booking between two real emergencies is left as a dispatch call for a person, not auto-shifted to an invalid hour.

rules.text: the 30-minute buffer between jobs exists for drive time between properties — back-to-back jobs at the SAME property (e.g. two units in the same building) need no buffer, since Justin is already on site. The buffer only applies between jobs at different properties. This applies everywhere a slot is searched, including the emergency shift above and the same-day gap-closing pass below.

plain brand-new repairs (no chat/pref/emergency trigger) are placed by building CODE PREFIX (e.g. "k104"), not pure priority+earliest-slot — the goal is Justin spending a whole day at one property instead of bouncing around. A new job first looks for an existing future day already dedicated to its property with room; if none, it starts a fresh day on the nearest completely open work day; if neither is possible within 90 days, it falls back to the plain earliest-slot search so nothing goes unscheduled. 1. **Declutter:** a day where no property has 2+ melds (every job is a lone stop) has zero clustering value — relocate its singles, one at a time, to any OTHER day that already has a real cluster of its own, regardless of destination property (a lone stop's drive time doesn't depend on which day it lands on). Never dumps into another weak/lone day or a completely empty one — that would just relocate the clutter instead of solving it. Frees the day entirely for a future same-property block to move into. 2. **Gap-fill:** pulls melds forward into a day's open tail time — (a) more of that day's own property from the nearest later day, (b) a complete different-property day/group that fits the gap entirely, (c) loose singles (priority, then oldest-created first), capped to one per source day (its current last job) so a pull never leaves a fresh gap behind. 3. **Same-property consolidation:** a property scattered across multiple days is merged onto whichever of those days already has the most of it, REBUILT from 8am — that property's block first (existing + pulled-in candidates that still fit), then any other-property filler that was already on that day. **Always respects the normal 4pm close (changed 2026-07-09)** — a candidate (or the filler after it) is only pulled in if the whole day still fits by 4pm; a property with too much volume for one day simply keeps its overflow elsewhere rather than stretching the day past close. (Previously allowed running to 6pm — Florencia, 2026-07-02 — but in practice that produced non-emergency days running to 6pm and dragged unrelated filler work past close too, so it was removed.) All three passes skip today, locked/preference melds, Emergency/Urgent, and — per Florencia, originally 2026-07-02, made a rolling window 2026-07-09 — **anything within the next 14 days of whenever it's run** (`FREEZE_WINDOW_DAYS` in `pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js`); the schedule-change window only covers dates beyond that 2-week horizon, so near-term work stays stable and the cutoff never goes stale between runs. Kept manual deliberately until it's been watched working correctly for a while — it moves already-scheduled jobs across dates, which is exactly what the "never move an already-scheduled date" rule above normally forbids.
details: **Past-due work does NOT cluster (2026-07-09):** a past-due job already carries a resident expectation from a prior date that fell through (e.g. the tech couldn't make it) — waiting for a "clean" property day to open up pushed these weeks out in practice (a real case landed a month away). Past-due jobs now take the nearest available slot on any day instead, same as a chat-driven reschedule — it can break that day's property theme for that one visit.

**Never moves the DATE of an already-scheduled job.** The only exception is same-day gap-closing (`sameDayCompaction`): every day is swept for gaps that no longer need to exist — a cancellation leaving a hole mid-day, or (since 2026-07-02) a same-property pair still carrying a buffer from before the property-aware rule existed — and the jobs after the gap (same day only, not preference-locked) shift earlier to close it. This is what replaced the old cross-day compaction, which used to undo clustering by pulling melds to the nearest open slot regardless of property.
Chat-driven reschedules and preference locks are unaffected by clustering — they keep their existing (higher-priority) behavior and can break a day's property theme for that one visit.
One-time backlog rebuild done 2026-07-01 via `pm_spokane_property_test.js` (kept in the repo as the reference implementation / for any future one-time re-clustering; not run automatically).

**Cross-day gap-filling (`pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js`, added 2026-07-02) — MANUAL only, not in any workflow.** A day that isn't fully booked 8am-4pm — including a completely empty workday sitting before later work — delays the backlog and eats an extra calendar day for no reason. Run this by hand (`DRY_RUN=1 node pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js` to preview, `node pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js` live). Three passes, in order:

rules.text: **David Sanchez and Alexander Overall** handle recurring "Lawn service" melds in Spokane (plus Our Natural Homes). Repairs and other techs' work are not touched.
Each week's recurring lawn melds are snapped to a **canonical template week** (a fixed day, time, and duration per property) and mirrored forward **+7 days**, so the times never drift week to week.
details: A property lands on the calendar as often as PropertyMeld generates its instance — most are weekly; a few (e.g. h731) are intentionally bi-weekly.

**h731 duplicate recurrence removed (2026-07-16):** h731 briefly had two PropertyMeld recurrences pointing at the same slot — one correct (every 15 days, id 163904) and one duplicate firing every 7 days (id 179920). Florencia deleted the 7-day one in PropertyMeld; the TEMPLATE in `pm_lawn_scheduler.js` now only maps the bi-weekly id.

**o155-Elm added to the template (2026-07-16, id 162926):** a separate recurrence from o155-Oak (162927) that had been running unscheduled/manual. Now fixed to Thursday 12:30 PM (1.25h), right after o155-Oak's slot ends.
A new recurrence not yet in the template is flagged as UNKNOWN so it can be added to the template.

rules.text: **Reynaldo Leonides ("Rey")** handles lawn, city-clustered: Mon+Tue kn47-K1 (two weekly blocks), Wed kn47-K1 "extras" (periodic items — bed weeding, irrigation checks, tree limb clearance, flower bed refresh, weed spraying — each has its own fixed Wednesday slot so simultaneous due-dates never overlap), Thu Richland (rl16 + rl21), Fri Pasco (ps17 + ps25 + ps91).
**Hannah Deckard** handles grounds/porter work: Tue Pasco, Wed Richland, Mon/Thu/Fri Kennewick (kn47 K1).

**Scope is deliberately narrow — recurring melds ONLY.** One-off melds for Rey/Hannah (sprinkler repairs, pest issues, bulk furniture, etc.) are always placed manually by Florencia or the tech — this scheduler never touches them, and has no Emergency/Urgent override logic (not needed since one-offs, where an emergency would live, are out of scope entirely).
**No Monday reserve** — unlike Tacoma/Spokane, Rey and Hannah work a normal Mon–Fri week (no emergency-driven Monday hold), same as Spokane's David/Alexander.
**Never touches the current week** — only schedules starting the Monday after the current week, same convention as the Spokane lawn template.

runs every 3 days, so it doesn't map to one fixed weekday like the rest of the template. It rotates through a fixed 3-slot cycle each time a new instance needs placing — Mon 06:00 → Wed 06:00 → Fri 10:15 → back to Mon — rather than a single fixed day. Hannah moves it by hand if the auto-picked day doesn't match actual need.

when a resident gives notice or moves out, AppFolio sets a move-out date and a **Standard Unit Turn** project is created in PropertyMeld for that unit. The turn's start date is the **day after the move-out date**. One turn per unit — duplicates are skipped.

Ron Cramer and Micheal Magoon do the in-house work (Scott Higley no longer works here). These are the **only two turn techs** — no additional hires (an earlier note claimed two more start July 20, 2026; that hire never happened — corrected 2026-07-17). Ron and Michael only do **maintenance and paint** — cleaning and flooring are vendors.

**2 back-to-back days of paint, then 1 day of maintenance**, all done by the **same tech** (one tech per unit). Plus a **1-hour initial walkthrough** the day after the unit vacates, split between both techs.

**Monday–Thursday, 8 AM–4 PM. Friday is left open** as a buffer for delays; no weekend work. A turn's paint→maintenance may bridge the Friday/weekend (e.g. paint Thursday + Monday). Both techs are kept fully booked Mon–Thu to finish turns as fast as possible.

applies **only to new, unscheduled turns** as they're added — it never re-orders or pulls forward turns already on the calendar (see the append-only rule in "General"). New turns are sequenced by a strict priority ladder: **(1) leased units first** (a new tenant is already lined up, so the move-in deadline is firm), by soonest move-in date; then **(2) units with a Converted application**, by earliest desired move-in date; then **(3) units with a Converting application**, by earliest desired move-in date; then **(4) highest property vacancy %**, to clear the most-affected properties fastest; then **(5) highest scheduled rent**. Only **Converted** and **Converting** applications count toward the desired-move-in tiers — **Converted always outranks Converting** — because those are the prospects actually likely to sign; every other application status is ignored for scheduling priority.

rules.category: Vendors (coming once the new techs start)
rules.text: cleaning (Spo Cleaning) is scheduled after paint and maintenance finish, with a **2-business-day buffer** (maintenance Monday → cleaning Thursday); carpet cleaning (Allklean) the day after cleaning; flooring/carpet replacement by Inland Pacific Flooring; the final walkthrough the day after carpet cleaning.

once the work is scheduled, the unit's **Available date and Ready-to-Show date are set to the same day**, and **Rent Ready is set to "No."** Only the turn manager sets Rent Ready to "Yes," as a verification step — the automation never does. The available date is **3 days after the final walkthrough** (a buffer for punch-list items found at the walkthrough or vendor delays); until the vendor steps are automated, it's an interim **7 days after maintenance is completed**.

**Cancelled move-out / notice-to-vacate → delete the turn (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-17).** If a unit's move-out or notice-to-vacate is cancelled (the resident is staying), that unit is no longer turning: the turn is **unscheduled** (all its PropertyMeld appointments cancelled) and the **turn project is removed completely** (its open melds and the project deleted). This frees the days it was holding on Ron/Magoon's calendars, and the next daily gap-fill run **fills that opening with the next-highest-priority unscheduled turn** (per the priority ladder above). This is the only case where already-scheduled in-house work is removed — it isn't a reschedule of valid work, it's reclaiming a slot for a turn that shouldn't exist anymore (so it stays consistent with the append-only rule).

AppFolio is checked **daily** for move-out dates that change or move-outs that get cancelled, and the turn schedule (and the available date) is updated to match. A cancelled move-out triggers the delete-the-turn rule above; a changed move-out date shifts the turn's start (new work is added per the append-only rule — existing placed work is not moved).
